title: HUSOVIC ET  AUTRES c. ITALIE
summary: In the case of Husovic and Others v. Italy, the applicants—Ms. Rasema Husovic, Mr. Dani Halilovic, and their daughters Indiana and Brigida Halilovic—were members of the Roma community from the former Yugoslavia, living in Rome. Their case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers facing repeated forced evictions and the destruction of their homes without proper legal safeguards or alternative accommodation. After arriving in Rome, the family settled in the Casilino 900 nomad camp and were registered during a 1995 census. In 1999, they moved to the Via Salone 323 camp, where they lived in a wooden house. On 4 August 2004, municipal authorities demolished their home as part of camp restructuring, and after the family rebuilt, their new house was again destroyed on 8 November 2004. The applicants alleged that these actions were carried out without administrative orders, compensation, or offers of alternative housing. They brought their complaint under Articles 3, 8, and 14 of the European Convention on Human Rights and Article 1 of Protocol No. 1. However, before the Court could rule on the merits, the applicants withdrew their complaint after being provided with suitable housing, and the case was struck out. This case reflects the ongoing challenges Roma and Traveller families face regarding housing rights and forced evictions in Europe, a persistent issue with deep historical roots.
